title: EKS provisioning: Terraform autosync heartbeat orchestrator for Private control plane
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
Build a lightweight Terraform 'autosync heartbeat orchestrator' that runs alongside the Private EKS control plane bootstrapper to detect and remediate configuration drift, surface preflight health signals, and coordinate safe staged upgrades for customer VPCs. This ticket implements the Terraform module glue + operator-compatible hooks so the orchestrator can safely call 'terraform plan/apply' in guarded windows and roll back if cluster-level health checks fail.

Why this exists:
- We continue to see manual remediation cycles for drift after upgrades and external infra changes (route tables, SGs, IAM roles).
- Existing preflight checks run only at bootstrap time; we need periodic verification plus an automated, auditable remediation path for small, non-disruptive fixes (eg. missing tags, drifted SG rules).

Scope (this ticket):
- Terraform module changes: add an S3 state-locking and state-diff export endpoint used by the autosync service; introduce a small, opt-in 'orchestrator' submodule with guard rails and dry-run mode.
- Orchestrator runner: a stateless controller (container) that runs as a CronJob/Deployment during rollout windows. It performs leader election, fetches remote state, runs terraform plan --detailed-exitcode, and if safe, triggers a guarded apply.
- Health probes: tie into existing control plane health endpoints and add an orchestration-level heartbeat metric (prometheus) + CloudWatch dashboard.
- Rollback policy: if the apply causes health regressions (measured by node readiness, control-plane API latency, and kube-apiserver error-rate SLOs), trigger automated rollback using the saved prior state snapshot and mark the attempt as failed with runbook link.
- Observability & Audit: every plan/apply run must write a compact execution record (who/what/when/diff) to the customer audit log and surface a permalink in the Console.

Non-goals:
- Full replacement of our existing provisioner operator. This is an augmentation to reduce manual fixes and provide safer, auditable remediations for common drift classes.

Acceptance criteria:
- The terraform module exposes a documented 'orchestrator' toggle and S3 path variables in examples (README updated).
- A deployable orchestrator container image that can run in customer Private control planes in 'dry-run' mode and 'apply' mode behind a feature flag.
- Leader election + single-active-run guarantee per control plane cluster.
- Plan runs produce a compact diff artifact and an exec record persisted to S3 (or internal audit store).
- If an apply introduces health regressions within 10 minutes, the orchestrator triggers rollback and posts an incident marker to the console.
- End-to-end e2e test that simulates a stuck SG rule causing drift and verifies that the orchestrator detects the drift and succeeds in remediation in 'apply' mode only when health checks pass.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We chose a periodic controller (CronJob) rather than a daemon to limit the risk window for automated applies. This reduces constant mutation surface area and makes audits simpler.
- Leader election uses our existing lease-based approach (Kubernetes Leases) so multiple orchestrators in a region don't run concurrently on the same customer cluster.
- Terraform runs happen in ephemeral pods with restricted IAM role via IRSA; we will not store long-lived credentials in the container.
- Drift remediations are split into two classes: non-disruptive (tags, metadata, small SG additions) and disruptive (node pool replacements). Only non-disruptive changes are auto-applied in the initial rollout.
- We will keep 'dry-run' as the default in orgs until runbooks and dashboards are validated.

Implementation steps:
1) Terraform module: add orchestrator submodule, S3 state export endpoint, tagging/metadata checks (3d).
2) Build orchestrator container: plan/apply driver, leader election, health-check hooks, and telemetry (4d).
3) Add e2e harness in CI: synthetic cluster scenario, inject drift, validate remediation and rollback (3d).
4) Console integration: execution record permalink, audit log ingestion (2d).
5) Run canary on internal staging org, gather metrics and adjust conservative rules (2d).

Testing and rollout plan:
- Local dev: test plan/apply flow against a small ephemeral cluster in our dev org.
- CI: run e2e harness on PRs to ensure deterministic behavior.
- Staging canary: enable 'apply' mode for 5 internal staging clusters for 1 week, monitor heuristics (apply success rate, rollback rate, health impact).
- Gradual customer opt-in: default to dry-run off; customers can opt in per-cluster and per-change-class via the module variable.

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: Automated applies could cause an outage if a normally-safe change is misclassified. Mitigation: conservative whitelisting of allowed change types, quick rollback snapshot, and 10-minute rollback window enforced.
- Risk: State conflicts between orchestrator and other tooling. Mitigation: use state locking and short TTL leases. Document required workflows for third-party IaC.
